title: Malformed input: raw clients send frames and inputs a real client never would while two rendered players play
description: map_01, enemies standing still and harmless (as S15). Two rendered clients play normally (one walks a circle, one walks back and forth) for the whole run. From 5 s a raw-client harness step (lab/rawprobe.py, lab/rawclient.py: gateway auth, enter world, KCP join, JSON envelopes) runs one case per fresh session: a length prefix over the 1 MiB frame limit (1048577 and 0xFFFFFFFF), a zero length, a truncated frame followed by silence, an envelope of an undefined type (99) and of an out-of-range type (300), a garbage protobuf envelope, a valid Input envelope with a garbage payload, out-of-range movement vectors (magnitudes 1.6, 50 and 1e6; GameConstants.MaxInputMagnitude is 1.5), attacks on an enemy beyond GameConstants.AttackRange, and casts of the first projectile ability at 10 per second (cooldown 45 ticks). Graded: the server process stays up and holds its tick; each case is refused or closes only the offending session (gameserver /status connections, gameserver_inputs_rejected_total{reason}, and every counter that moved are in the report; the undefined-type case has no server-side signal and grades INCONCLUSIVE); the rendered clients see no session change and no snapshot gap over 250 ms.

assertions.title: the game server never restarts and always answers /status
the server holds its tick rate while it is fed garbage
every malformed case is refused or closes only the offending session

unknown_type.note: The server has no counter or log line for an undefined message type (GameServer.cs OnMessageReceived default arm logs at Debug; Program.cs sets the console minimum level to Information), so this case is INCONCLUSIVE until the server counts it: staying connected does not show the input was refused or ignored.

assertions.title: the rendered clients see no session close
the rendered clients see no snapshot gap over the S01 threshold
